entries.name: Deterministic preference compliance oracle
entries.focus: Proving that stated operator preferences actually change agent behaviour
entries.situation: You inject operator preferences into every turn and have no evidence they bind. Especially valuable when that injection is expensive: here it cost ~2,573 tokens per user turn and ~5,772 at session start, and the only prior evidence was the agent grading itself (64% self-scored adherence, which is the defendant's testimony).
entries.anti_situation: You inject few or no preferences, or you are content with self-assessment. Also a poor fit if you expect broad coverage: most preferences cannot be adjudicated by any deterministic rule, and this reports them UNMEASURABLE rather than inventing a score. Coverage here is 13 detectors against 118 preferences and that is the honest ceiling, not a defect to fix.
entries.cost: One detector function per measurable preference; runs over transcripts, no model calls, negligible tokens.
entries.value_note: The load-bearing rule: no model judges anything. A detector proves a violation by pointing at the offending characters, or abstains. entries.name: Savepoint trail as a walkable audit path
entries.focus: Re-checking whether past work still does what it claimed
entries.situation: You want to know if work from weeks ago still holds, without paying a model to re-read history and form an opinion. entries.name: Assurance loop — instrument findings become dispatchable work
entries.focus: Closing the gap between measuring and acting
entries.situation: You have health instruments nobody looks at. If your dispatch engine acts on work items rather than reports, a finding that never becomes a work item is invisible however correct it is. This runs the instruments and writes each finding into the backlog in the only form the engine can act on.
entries.anti_situation: You have no automated dispatch, or fewer than two instruments — then a human reading the output directly is simpler and better. Also skip if your backlog is already unmanageable: this ADDS items, and an ignored queue plus more items is worse.

entries.name: Claim-is-not-evidence gate on completion records
entries.focus: Preventing self-assertion from entering the durable record
entries.situation: Your completion records carry a verified flag that any agent can set by writing the word. This rejects verified=true unless the entry records something a machine can RE-RUN later: a command, a path, or a commit sha. Prose is a note, not evidence.

prerequisites: structured completion records with a verified field
replaces: trusting a verified flag at face value

entries.name: Shared database project until there are real users
entries.focus: Controlling cost and resisting over-building early
entries.situation: A new or pre-launch spoke needing a database. Use the SHARED supabase project rather than provisioning an isolated one. Cheaper, faster to stand up, and nothing about an unused schema justifies its own project. This is a capability whose value is PREVENTING work — the wheel must be able to advocate not building yet, not only advocate building.
entries.anti_situation: The spoke has real users, or holds data whose loss or exposure would matter, or has compliance/isolation requirements. At that point shared is the wrong answer and the companion card applies.
entries.cost: Near zero to adopt. Deferred cost is a later schema relocation, which is why the follow-up card exists.
prerequisites: a shared supabase project available to the wheel

entries.name: Relocate schema to a dedicated project once there are real users
entries.focus: Escaping shared infrastructure at the right moment
entries.situation: The spoke has crossed into real users. Recommend relocating its schema from the shared supabase project to a dedicated one: isolation, independent scaling, and blast-radius containment now justify the cost that was unjustifiable a month earlier.
entries.anti_situation: Still pre-launch, or usage is incidental/internal. Relocating early pays the cost with none of the benefit, which is the over-building this pair exists to prevent.
entries.cost: A schema migration plus a dedicated project's running cost.
entries.verification: manual — confirm the spoke's schema is on its own project
falsification_cases: must NOT fire on a spoke that never left pre-launch

antipatterns.schema_note: Anti-patterns modeled as MEASURABLE negative capabilities (impl-antipattern-coverage-probe-v1): each entry pairs a captured symptom/root_cause with a DETECT oracle (a command + expected exit code) so 'did we drive it out?' is a per-spoke pass/fail, not an assertion. `detect.cmd` may use {spoke_path}/{hub_path} placeholders, substituted the same way capability_runner.py substitutes them for capabilities-base.json commands. enforced_by names the tool/function that is supposed to keep the anti-pattern from recurring; teaching_id links the auto-memory/teaching that first captured it (null if none yet); since_version is the harness version the enforcement shipped in.

entries.symptom: A managed-file edit lands and passes review, but distribution never picks it up — MANIFEST.json's recorded md5 still points at the old bytes, so the fix is authored but never actually reaches any spoke.
entries.root_cause: spoke/managed/** was edited without recutting MANIFEST.json (manifest_build.py), so the manifest silently drifted from the on-disk managed tree.

judgement_summary.convention: Cards split into machine-DERIVED facts (paths, symbols, existence — regenerated, never read as intent) and asserted JUDGEMENT (situation, anti_situation, cost, value — carries an author and a date). A foreign Ozi must be able to tell them apart.
judgement_summary.note: Coverage is not the goal. A small set of real cards beats universal coverage of hollow ones.
judgement_summary.coverage_note: Tools and hooks were registered 2026-07-19 after an audit found 0 of 195 tools and 0 of 18 hooks in the graph — the pre-existing audit tool was scoped to COMMANDS by design. Tools carry the actual behaviour of this variant, so a lineage reading only our commands saw almost nothing of it. Presence is now complete; JUDGEMENT is deliberately sparse and labelled rather than fabricated.
judgement_summary.tiers_note: Cards now span three tiers: machinery (what exists), build-preference (the operator's strongly-held defaults, including ones that PREVENT work), and mandate (applied, not weighed).
